card: Catches std::runtime_error in CreateWallet so external signer setup failures return error messages instead of aborting bitcoin-qt on an unhandled exception. It also cleans up newly created wallet database files and directories when creation fails, preventing subsequent attempts using the same wallet name from failing with 'Database already exists'. Over RPC, failed setups now cleanly return RPC_WALLET_ERROR (-4) instead of an unhandled exception code (-1).
evidence: PR description: 'On master: terminate called after throwing an instance of std::runtime_error, the process aborts, and trezor_t/wallet.dat is left behind.'
PR description notes this uncaught exception was previously reported in bitcoin-core/gui#395.
problem: When external signer setup fails during wallet creation, an uncaught `std::runtime_error` terminates the GUI process because worker threads lack exception handlers. Additionally, failed wallet creation attempts leave behind partially initialized database files and directories, preventing users from retrying creation with the same wallet name due to 'Database already exists' errors.

risk.why: A flaw in the cleanup logic could erroneously remove pre-existing user files or directories upon a failed wallet creation attempt.

summary: Wraps `CWallet::CreateNew` in a try-catch block within `CreateWallet` to handle `std::runtime_error` exceptions during wallet initialization, such as external signer failures. Upon any wallet creation failure, it removes newly created database files and directories using non-throwing filesystem calls. It also changes the RPC failure code for these setup errors from -1 to `RPC_WALLET_ERROR` (-4).
